2
The maximum theoretical power P of a wind turbine is given by the equation
P = kρAv n
where ρ is the density of air, A is the area swept by the turbine blades, v is the speed of the air
and k is a constant with no units.
What is the value of n ?
A
1
B
2
C
3
D
4

hints: Write the SI base units for power $P$ as $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3}$ and for $\rho$, $A$ and $v$ as $\text{kg m}^{-3}$, $\text{m}^2$ and $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Substitute these units into $P = k\rho A v^n$, remembering $k$ has no units, so the units of $\rho A v^n$ must equal the units of $P$.
Compare the powers of $\text{s}$ on both sides: $\text{s}^{-3}$ must equal $\text{s}^{-n}$, then check the powers of $\text{m}$ to confirm.
walkthrough: Recall the base units: power $P$ is $\text{W} = \text{J s}^{-1} = \text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3}$, density $\rho$ is $\text{kg m}^{-3}$, area $A$ is $\text{m}^2$, and speed $v$ is $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
For homogeneity the units must balance: $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3} = (\text{kg m}^{-3})(\text{m}^2)(\text{m s}^{-1})^n$ because $k$ is dimensionless.
Simplify the right-hand side: $(\text{kg m}^{-3})(\text{m}^2) = \text{kg m}^{-1}$, and $(\text{m s}^{-1})^n = \text{m}^n \text{s}^{-n}$, giving $\text{kg m}^{n-1} \text{s}^{-n}$.
Check with powers of $\text{m}$: $2 = n - 1$ also gives $n = 3$, confirming consistency.

A.explanation: With $n=1$, the right-hand side has units of $\text{kg s}^{-1}$, not power.

B.explanation: With $n=2$, the right-hand side has units of $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, which is force, not power.

C.explanation: With $n=3$, the right-hand side has units of $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3}$, which matches power $P$.

D.explanation: With $n=4$, the right-hand side has units of $\text{kg m}^3 \text{s}^{-4}$, which is too large by $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
